items.body: Black Bordello’s latest single, Numb-Lock, is a song that begins in a theatre of injury, but its drama is never decorative. The London art-rock group, led by Sienna Bordello, treats excess as a form of precision: operatic singing, gothic glamour, piano-room grandeur, and lyrics that peer into psychic damage without turning it into costume. Here, the band narrows its aim. The subject is physical abuse, inflicted by a former friend, and the strange afterlife of the body once trust has been turned into threat. Numb-Lock is concerned less with spectacle than with the slow return of sensation: the frozen mind, the private inventory of harm, the labor of self-protection when the danger has passed but the body has kept its own evidence. Bordello sings with an almost formal control, allowing emotion to gather through restraint rather than volume alone. Her soprano can recall Kate Bush’s bright altitude, Kristeen Young’s melodrama, and Siouxsie Sioux’s theatrical command, though its force here comes from the way she lets beauty carry dread without sweetening it. The arrangement has the broad, dangerous elegance of a Bond theme, but Black Bordello gives that scale a bruised interior. Classical flourishes rise against post-punk undertow; the song moves with ceremony, yet its emotional motion is jagged, as if each grand entrance must first pass through a locked room. Altsach’s production gives the instruments enough space to loom without crowding the central performance. When the track swells, the effect is architectural: arches, chandeliers, cracked plaster, a voice standing in the middle, too exacting for easy rescue. Produced by Balazs Altsach, the single takes the shape of an orchestral post-punk ballad, built for velvet curtains and hard facts, with strings and bass pressure moving around Bordello’s voice as if the room were being rearranged by memory itself. Numb-Lock suggests that a band’s most powerful work often may come when the music is made to serve a wound, and the wound is allowed to speak in a voice large enough to survive it. Listen to the song below, or via the band’s streaming page here: Since forming after the pandemic, Black Bordello have built a career on theatrical risk. They have shared stages with The Libertines, Goat Girl, Fat Dog, and Pete Doherty, while recent appearances at Left of the Dial and New Colossus have placed them in a wider transatlantic frame. With a third album drawing attention, and 2026 dates including London’s 100 Club, Kendal Calling, Oslo, Berlin’s 8mm Festival, and selected shows supporting David J, Black Bordello are moving with unusual assurance, gathering baroque ambition into something hard, lucid, and oddly intimate. Follow Black Bordello: Instagram TikTok YouTube Facebook Website The post London’s Black Bordello Delivers Dark, Wounded Elegance With Bond-Theme Ballad “Numb-Lock” appeared first on Post-Punk.com.
items._cn_summary: Black Bordello 是来自伦敦的后朋克/哥特艺术摇滚乐队，单曲《Numb-Lock》将后朋克的暗潮质感与管弦乐宏大编曲相融合，呈现出类似邦德主题曲的剧场化优雅。女主唱 Sienna Bordello 的高音兼具有 Kate Bush 的高远、Siouxsie Sioux 的戏剧张力与 Kristeen Young 的夸张，演唱方式克制而精准。制作人 Balazs Altsach 的编曲让古典弦乐与后朋克低音之间形成张力，歌曲结构充满仪式感却不流于浮夸。题材聚焦身体虐待与创伤后的感官回归，歌词与音乐之间的咬合紧密。整体在暗潮、哥特与当代古典的交汇处形成了具有辨识度的声音，属于独立场景中跨类型融合的扎实之作。

items.body: Eyes wide weary to a midday sun Oh! what could have been The Monolithic slab of this endless drab We’re living, in the cracks between NAUT’s latest single, Liberation, comes barging out of Bristol as both a warning flare and a love letter to the goth club as a sanctuary: a room set against the technocratic nightmare of compliance, optimization, surveillance, and dead-eyed productivity. Outside, the world measures, manages, and flattens the self into data. Inside, under low light and heavy sound, outsiders gather, move, and become whole. That opposition sits at the heart of goth itself. Gothic romanticism has always been the enemy of clean systems and obedient surfaces, answering utility with mystery, control with desire, productivity with ritual, and rational order with the unruly intelligence of grief, beauty, fear, and longing. For NAUT, this is no abstract pose. The band were born on goth dancefloors around the world, forged in the spaces where the strange find recognition, and where night offers a freedom the day cannot authorize. Liberation treats the night as a force of release: the hour when fear loosens, false selves fall away, and the dark night of the soul becomes a kind of transformation. The track confronts both personal darkness and the wider machinery of control and compliance, treating inner turmoil and outside pressure as parts of the same struggle. Its death-rock heft comes across as disciplined rather than gaudy, with coldwave restraint folded into a thicker, more physical frame. The guitars descend in heavy black planes, sharpened at the edges, while the synthesizers sit at a glacial remove, throwing the bass into relief. Beneath it all, the drum machine advances with bureaucratic menace, each strike suggesting the dull violence of systems that never need to raise their voice. The lyrics to Liberation aim their anger at the systems that shape modern life: work targets, digital metrics, managed desire, and the dead-screen obedience of a world lived through devices. NAUT set private ambition and historical burden inside that same tightening mechanism, where the self is measured, monitored, and made useful until little remains but exhaustion and performance. The song treats the daylight world as a monolithic slab of endless drab, a regime of polished surfaces, shrinking choices, and constant compliance, where the human soul is expected to survive in the cracks between. Against that machinery, the club becomes a counter-institution: a place where the body is no longer something to discipline, optimize, or make productive, but something to release. The chorus rises with the severe grandeur of a vaulted ceiling, while the bassline keeps the song locked to the floor, reminding us that transcendence can begin with movement, with hips, shoulders, boots, and bodies finding freedom together before anything reaches the heavens. The DIY video, filmed in Bristol, sharpens this idea by refusing elaborate explanation in favour of pressure, performance, and nocturnal momentum. It carries the charge of a horror film opening in real time, less through plot than through atmosphere: bodies caught in artificial light, faces moving through darkness, the band appearing as both witnesses and accelerants. Watch the video for Liberation below: Following the release of Hunt, and after tours alongside Creeper, The March Violets, She Past Away, and Katatonia, NAUT sound tighter, meaner, and more club-minded here. Liberation is gothic post-punk built for boots on sticky floors, for mascara running by choice, and for freedom from the status quo. Listen to Liberation below, and order the single here. items.body: The history of America is haunted by ghosts of the past. These ghosts transform our present-day landscape, our everyday lives, and inform the very core of our existence. On Alive With Ghosts Today (Edition Records, 2026), saxophonist Chris Potter steps away from the normal high-adrenaline jazz that has signified his recent outings and has instead put together a band designed to feel more like a small-town ensemble, a mixture of jazz and folk, to lead through a suite of tunes that examines the legacy of abolitionist John Brown and his raid on Harpers Ferry in 1859 and begs to ask the question: what have we learned, what can we learn, why are we still, wrestling with these same ghosts from the past? The ensemble Potter has assembled is the key to the album's success. Bill Frisell plays with a spacious grace that wonderfully supports all the musicians. Frisell blends in seamlessly, sliding between the other instruments and adding his own unique voice to the music; his guitar serves as the counterpoint to Potter's lead lines. It is hard to believe that although drummer Nate Smith has played with Potter for many years, this is the first time he has worked with Frisell, they are intuitively locked in as if they had been playing together for years. Bassist Burniss Travis brings a loose, funky "groove" to the proceedings, providing a fluid anchor alongside Smith to form a formidable rhythm section. Potter's playing throughout is profound; he is not just playing; he is issuing a warning that the same discontent that fueled the fire that led to Brown's failed raid to free the enslaved people at Harper's Ferry is still smoldering beneath the surface of society today. On "Osawatomie Brown," the addition of Sara Caswell on violin, Rane Moore on clarinet and Zekkereya El-magharbel on trombone transforms the band from a traditional jazz quartet into something much more strongly suited to the historical weight of the song, adding a sense of tension to the music, almost as if they were a Greek chorus, answering Potter's playing, commenting on it. They bring a mournful, melancholic sound to the song, haunting and passing judgment on the unfolding events of the unsuccessful raid, as Brown now must face the consequences of leading the failed rebellion. Brown's final words before his execution serve as a grim warning that is as true today as it was then. "I, John Brown, am now quite certain that the crimes of this guilty land will never be purged away but with blood." In fact, Potter's suite does not so much as play out as a tribute to Brown, but serves as a haunting reminder that these ghosts are still very alive and relevant today. Potter's weary tone throughout the album points to his disbelief that 167 years after Brown's failed raid on Harpers Ferry, we are still caught up in an endless cycle of conflict, doomed to repeat the failures of the past until we rectify the present. Alive With Ghosts Today is not an easy listen, not because it is not a good album; in fact, it is a triumph of artistic vision, but because it demands the listener to do more than "listen." It is a thought-provoking statement from one of the great artists of today, passing judgment on society through the lens of examining the past and demanding that we act to finally put those ghosts to rest so that we can positively impact the society of both today and tomorrow.
items._cn_summary: 萨克斯演奏家Chris Potter策划的概念爵士组曲专辑，以美国废奴主义者John Brown及其1859年哈普斯渡口袭击事件为核心叙事，融合爵士与民谣元素。阵容包括吉他手Bill Frisell、鼓手Nate Smith、贝斯手Burniss Travis组成的四重奏，以及小提琴、 clarinet与长号构成的室内乐编制，赋予作品历史厚重感与希腊合唱般的叙事张力。整张专辑在爵士即兴框架下融入民谣的质朴与室内乐的庄严，以音乐回应社会议题，呈现学院派爵士的概念化探索。Edition Records为英国独立厂牌，发行定位偏向小众与艺术化路线。

items.body: Feebles, Fables and Ferns captures a rare duo session between guitarist Mick Goodrick and pianist Fred Hersch. Recorded in August 1988 at Hersch's studio in New York, the album provides an intimate display of the superbly matched improvisational skills of two musicians in full flight. During his career, Goodrick perfected the art of avoiding the spotlight, even when collaborating with artists such as John Surman, Charlie Haden and Gary Burton. He was not prolific as a composer or recording artist, preferring to work behind the scenes, often in educational roles. Yet his innovative approach to improvisation proved influential, with many prominent musicians, among them Julian Lage and Pat Metheny, acknowledging his impact. For over three decades, Hersch's work as a pianist, composer and collaborator has resulted in over 60 albums, either as a leader or co-leader, along with multiple Grammy nominations and a host of awards. He is internationally recognized as one of jazz's most distinctive voices. The album opens with the title track. This was composed by Goodrick and was originally recorded on his debut album In Passing (ECM, 1979). The guitar opens the track, Hersch joins, and soon the instruments are intertwined, spinning and folding solo lines around, each leaving spaces for the other to explore as they move through an array of moods. Hersch's composition "Heartsong" is the central track. The piece has previously been featured in trio format on his 1990 album Heartsongs (Sunnyside) and on his 2001 solo album Songs Without Words (Nonesuch Records). In the duo's hands, the piece becomes a harmonic delight, the instruments exchanging the melody to captivating effect. The whole album is an exercise in listening and responding. This reaches its height on the spontaneous improvisations of "Five Excursions." As Hersch notes, "The highlight to me is just the level of ensemble playing. There was a lot of profound listening going on between the both of us." Alongside the originals are four covers. "Falling Grace" and "Amazing" are both Steve Swallow compositions, with the latter leading in with Goodrick's "Away 10." Its beautiful unfolding melody and improvised passages form another highlight. Johnny Green and Edward Heyman's "Out Of Nowhere" sees melodic fragments eventually merge and Goodrick's solo shimmers through Mal Waldron's "Soul Eyes." These two musicians are so well matched that they conjure something close to magic in this intimate studio session. They interweave their lines, expanding and contracting to build delicate miniatures, tender melodic exchanges and romantic drifts. But there is energy here too, making this pure musical communication of the highest order.

items._cn_summary: 这张1977年的首张专辑记录了年仅22岁的Michael Gregory Jackson与三位自由爵士名家Oliver Lake、David Murray及Wadada Leo Smith的合作。音乐以中后期自由爵士为根基，融合爵士融合乐、新古典主义与弗拉门戈元素，呈现出超越年龄的成熟与实验性。作品中自由爵士段落、即兴抒情段落与弗拉门戈律动交织，编曲展现出复杂织体和跨类型探索的野心。作为一位年轻乐手的首张专辑，其音乐语言已具备相当的先锋意识和融合广度，是自由爵士向多元领域拓展的早期范例。

items.body: Skullflower’s band-mind ’92 noise rock salvo for JK Broadrick’s label is back to infect the water table on its 30th anniversary repress, newly augmented with a 2nd disc of extra, unreleased cuts from the same recording sessions - prime, atonal gnarl for disciples of Godflesh, Broken Flag, Fushitsusha Originally recorded in London, 1991, and released on Justin “Godflesh” Broadrick’s hEADdIRt in ’92, ‘IIIrd Gatekeeper’ marks the point when Matthew Bower (guitar), Anthony Di Franco (bass) and Stuart Dennison’s (drums, vocals) Skullflower were three years deep into their thing, and hailed among the world’s heaviest... more
items._cn_summary: 这是英国地下噪音摇滚乐队Skullflower于1991年录制、1992年由Godflesh主脑Justin Broadrick旗下厂牌hEADdIRt发行的经典专辑《IIIrd Gatekeeper》三十周年再版，额外收录同期未发表的录音。音乐以无调性、极度粗糙的吉他噪音为核心，融合工业音乐的力量感与自由即兴的实验精神，承袭Broken Flag与Fushitsusha等地下噪音传统。三位成员——吉他手Matthew Bower、贝斯Anthony Di Franco与鼓手Stuart Dennison——以三人编制制造出密度极高、压迫感强烈的声响景观。再版追加第二碟补充素材，为乐迷提供更完整的创作脉络。整体定位于极端实验噪音与小众工业交叉地带，是九十年代初英国地下场景的代表性作品之一。

items._cn_summary: 意大利电影配乐大师埃尼欧·莫里科内为帕索里尼1975年争议电影《萨罗，或索多玛120天》创作的原声，由专注于工业、暗黑氛围与实验音乐的独立厂牌Cold Spring发行。莫里科内在这部配乐中采用了大量先锋与实验手法，不协和音与极简手法营造出极度不安的氛围，与影片的极端主题形成呼应。Cold Spring以暗黑实验厂牌著称，此前已发行过《解码者》及Psychic TV的配乐作品，此次将一部具有历史地位的先锋电影配乐纳入其厂牌体系。该作品融合了当代古典的编配思维与实验音乐的声响逻辑，作为1970年代意大利激进电影美学的组成部分，在电影配乐史上占有独特地位，适合关注实验、先锋与暗黑氛围/工业音乐的听众。

items._cn_summary: Sa Pa是一位深耕地下电子音乐场景的制作人，创作脉络横跨dub techno、俱乐部techno与ambient、声音设计领域。《Girls on Tour EP》是他自创厂牌Dub Techno For Life的首发作品，收录四首曲目，呈现出质感细密、节奏压迫感强烈的声响特质。该EP将强劲的俱乐部舞曲基底与更具实验性的氛围探索并置，体现出从舞池功能到沉思空间的完整光谱。Sa Pa此前在Short Span与Astral Industries等独立厂牌均有发表，此作被视为其个人艺术面貌的集中呈现。整体定位介于经典Chain Reaction式dub techno传统与当代声音实验之间，适合偏好地下电子与实验声响交汇的听众。

items._cn_summary: 这是Max D（Andrew Field-Pickering）与Co La（Matt Papich）的第五张合作专辑，将即兴爵士、dub与后摇滚音景融合，并融入电影拟音手法与具体音乐元素，呈现出拼贴式的声音美学。专辑邀请了多位实验音乐人参演，延续了两人在PAN和Future Times等独立厂牌时期的实验脉络。前作《Trellis》以超现实录音拼贴著称，本作进一步将电影制作的思维方式引入音乐创作，跨界于自由即兴、电子声响与声音艺术之间，对实验音乐和前卫爵士听众具有较高吸引力。独立厂牌发行保障了创作自由度，但乐评原文被截断，音乐细节描述有限。

Interpreting that in sound isn't easy, so Suzuki stays relatively abstract, hiding her intentions behind droning, harmonic clouds, melancholy breaths that sound as if they're trapped... more
items._cn_summary: 东京艺术家铃木绫美（Ayami Suzuki）以专辑《Remnants》追忆已故父亲，将逝者遗留的情感痕迹转化为模糊而饱含情绪的氛围声响。作品以持续低音与和声层叠构建抽象音场，呼吸般的旋律片段隐约浮现，整体笼罩在忧郁而内省的氛围之中。乐评将其与William Basinski、Celer和Lawrence English等氛围/无人机音乐人并列，定位于当代实验氛围领域，侧重以抽象手法处理悲伤与存在的主题。作品融合了氛围音乐的环境质感与当代古典的冥想特质，适合偏好实验声响与情感氛围交叉领域的听众。

items._cn_summary: 这张合辑由巴西独立厂牌Lugar Alto发行，由GG Albuquerque策划、Akira Umeda混音，收录了来自里约热内卢和圣保罗声音系统文化中自1980年代至今的DJ宣传语与电台标识音效。Paredão是巴西特有的巨型音响系统文化，合辑以此为核心，梳理了巴西放克声音系统的演变脉络。从类型定位来看，它处于电子音乐、世界音乐与声音系统亚文化的交汇地带，以档案式策展的方式呈现巴西地下音乐景观中独特的声音碎片。整体概念偏向声音考古与文化记录，具有一定的实验性与地域研究价值，但原始评论内容较为简短，信息深度有限。

items._cn_summary: 这张EP由Alex Nut策划，汇聚了来自英国当代爵士乐坛的乐手——包括曾与Lianne La Havas合作的键盘手Sam Crowe、与Sault/Cleo Sol合作的打击乐手Junior Ali-Balogun，以及Kokoroko的贝斯手Duane Atherley，以Sum Of Its Parts之名呈现两首作品。主打曲《The Message》时长约八分钟，在爵士即兴的律动中铺展沉郁氛围，向深空式的爵士意境延展；《Hello High》则收紧结构，引入底特律式碎拍house律动，呼应Moodymann与Theo Parrish的经典美学。Brussels音乐人Boddhi Satva负责混音版本，为EP注入中部非洲血统的律动感知。整体定位介于学院派爵士与地下电子舞曲之间，是英国新派爵士场景与底特律跳舞音乐传统的对话。

Out of earshot for a minute, Voices From the Lake regroup around familiar aquatic themes on the satisfyingly immersive ‘II’. Signature Italian sound sensitivity and attention to spatialized detail meets subtle rhythmic urges for an hour of slowed, aquaplaning groove and crystal clear tone

Signature Italian sound sensitivity and attention to spatialized detail meets subtle rhythmic urges for an hour of slowed, aquaplaning groove and crystal clear tones that dive off from deep ends of ‘80s new age ambient, and its ‘90s techno descendants, into an elemental sound world idealised for... more
items._cn_summary: Voices From The Lake是意大利制作人Donato Dozzy与Neel合作的氛围电子项目，暌违十三年后推出的第二张专辑。作品延续了二人标志性的水系主题与意大利式声音美学，将八十年代新世纪氛围音乐与九十年代科技舞曲的基因相融合，营造出沉缓、流动的水下式律动。空间感处理细腻，音色清澈剔透，以环绕式声场构建出沉浸感强烈的声音景观。整体风格偏向氛围科技舞曲的纵深探索，强调质感与空间维度而非节奏驱动，适合专注聆听的小众电子场景。乐评指出其忠实再现了既有配方，在创新性上略显保守，但制作水准与氛围营造依然扎实。

items.excerpt: MBM carves three slow-burning studies in tension and release – merging patterns with fragile harmonics, melancholia, and restraint. "Everything feels carefully placed yet emotionally exposed. Moments of pressure give way to space, steel meets softness, rhythm turns inward. No peaks. No breaks. Just pulse, texture, and tone – in constant negotiation. Music for the body, drawn from the depths. Soultones hits hard. Feel it." more

items._cn_summary: 该专辑收录三首缓慢展开的张力与释放之作，将循环节奏模式与脆弱泛音相融合，整体笼罩在忧郁与克制的气质中。编曲强调精确与留白的平衡，情绪外露却不失控制，紧张压力与呼吸空间交替出现，金属质感与柔软音色交织，节奏趋向内敛。作品没有传统意义上的高潮与断裂，持续在脉动、质感与音色的协商中推进。声音设计偏向实验电子与氛围音乐领域，融入了泛音处理与极简律动，适合关注实验、前卫及暗潮质感的听众。专辑由独立厂牌发行，定位偏向小众聆听场景。

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由Echospace厂牌的Stephen Hitchell以Intrusion名义创作，是深沉的Dub Techno与氛围电子作品。音乐以绵延的低频、弥漫的混响和催眠式的节奏构建出朦胧的声场，适合长时间沉浸聆听。Pole负责重制母带处理，强化了空间层次与氛围感。整体风格接近Maurizio、GAS一系的氛围极简主义，属于地下电子音乐场景中典型的氛围Dub House再版作品，重在冥想式聆听体验而非结构创新。

items._cn_summary: Boards of Canada 1995年首张专辑《Twoism》再次进入流通视野。专辑最初仅以100张限量形式在独立厂牌Music70发行，后经Skam与Warp合作重新面世。这张作品奠定了二人组在IDM与氛围电子领域的重要地位，融合了低保真采样、怀旧音色与催眠式节拍，呈现出介于氛围、抽象嘻哈与电子民谣之间的独特声响美学。Warp作为电子音乐领域的标志性独立厂牌，为该作品提供了与其实验精神契合的发行平台。但本文更偏向于发行历史与收藏价值的资讯介绍，对音乐本身的声响特征与创作手法缺乏深入分析。

items._cn_summary: Mermaid是一位日本电子制作人，将数码dub、雷鬼dub与室内乐、当代古典以及日本传统民谣进行大胆融合。这张专辑对巴赫、戈塞克等古典作品以及日本传统歌曲进行了dub风格的重构，以正弦波塑形的低频线条和棱角分明的旋律线为特征。整张作品游走于dub的厚重低音与古典室内乐的精致织体之间，呈现出跨文化、跨类型的实验气质。来自日本这一非主流音乐场景的制作人将本土传统素材与西方古典经典并置，展现出独特的文化视角和艺术想象力。

items.body: 6YPAH (spreek uit als Buran) haalt zijn naam bij het Russische ruimteprogamma al komt de band wel uit Slovenië. Opgericht in 2008 start het duo Jani Toplaki en Giorgio Multineddu (Italiaan van geboorte) het rommelen met analoge synths om later gitaar en andere instrumenten toe te voegen en tot een eigen post punk, new wave taal te komen. Van alle projecten bij Final Muzik moet deze 6YPAH zowat het meest toegankelijke zijn. Het zal tot in 2023 duren vooraleer er fysiek materiaal, “Electronic Visions Across The Border” verschijnt in eigen beheer en nu is er deze “Prozorno Mesta” (te vertalen als transparante stad), dat in 2025 verscheen maar nu dus wordt opgepikt door het Final Muzik label. Wat ik hoor zijn zes, eerder poppy verpakte post punk songs, die uitgerust met een elektronische ruggengraat, zowel genres als post punk, new wave tot dark wave aftasten. Dat resulteert in een moderne Kraftwerk (ehum) track als “Supersila” die bol staat van synth pop ivloeden tot een typische post punk / dark wave track als “Neugörz”, een jonge, moderne stad in het westen van Slovenië, direct gelegen aan de grens met de Italiaanse stad Gorizia, waar de wieg van 6YPAH staat. In “Supersila” krijgt wijlen Ronald Reagan een hoofdrol. Politiek en maatschappij, het zou een vak in elke school moeten zijn, is het duo alvast niet vreemd getuige ook de titel “Distopija” waarmee het eindresultaat van de utopie kapitalisme en de utopie communisme wordt samengevat op een ietwat gelaten, vereenzaamde synth lijn. “‘Ustanova” (rust) waarmee het album opent kent een lange aanloop die naar kraut rock lijkt te lonken om eens over de drie minuten ietwat wispelturig een post punk steegje in te duiken en te eindigen met een soort kanarie robots die een ‘endzeit’ riedel tsjierpen. De meest romantische nummers “Veno S Tabo” (te vertalen als ‘altijd bij je’) en Pod Nebom (te vertalen als ‘onder de hemel') kennen in de verte een Molchat Doma Echo. Wat dit album, of moet ik met (slechts) zes nummers eerder over een uit de kluiten gewassen ep spreken, aangenaam om luisteren maakt is dat elk nummer weer net anders klinkt waardoor “Prozorno Mesta” nooit gaat vervelen maar de volle 29 minuten interessant blijft in een eigenzinnige mix van synth pop, new wave en post punk. Naar Final Muzik normen dus een zeer toegankelijke release van een bij ons totaal onbekend duo 6YPAH. Liefhebbers van ‘zachte’ post punk moeten dit zeker eens proberen. Prozorno Mesto by 6YPAH 6YPAH

items.body:
Home/Reviews/Accident Fantôme
ACCIDENT FANTÔME — OBJETS ENCHÂSSÉS DANS DES ANNEAUX PLANÉTAIRES( OBJECTS EMBEDDED IN A PLANETARY RING )
[moli del tro — 2026]
★
★
★
★
★
Reviewed 5 June 2026
by Colin Lang
Artist website →

Accident Fantôme is the portmanteau for the project of two otherwise autonomous, established musical duos, Accident du Travail and Fantôme Josepha. United by shared interests in historical instruments and long-form, ambient drone composition, the four gathered in an old church in a village just west of Metz (where some of the group are based) early last year to perform and record together.

The ecclesiastical setting was selected for its mid-19th-century pipe organ — the instrument par excellence of the dronies — along with its remoteness, outside of the hustle and bustle, though situated near the Front of the First World War and all its spectres. In addition to said organ, Objects Embedded in a Planetary Ring features guitar, harp, and the ondes Martenot, one of the earliest electric instruments, which, following in its use by Messiaen, Boulez, and others, has become something of a cult object among French classicists.

“Cosmos“: the opening track, is a swirl of harp and organ, pulling heavenward with little to no anchor, so that when an electric guitar struts its way into the mix, we get a bit more electronics and processing along with it. The whole thing is drowning in reverb, whether added through effects or culled from the church environs, it makes for an engrossing if familiar haze. “Euphorie”, the longest of the five compositions, leans pretty heavily into the organ, a single chord depressed, vibrating and blanketing the empty space into which it moans. Here, we get the clearest picture of the theremin-like whirling of the ondes Martenot, which takes us out of the house of worship and onto Mars. All of this ushers in some higher frequency squeaks before Brother Pipes takes control of the party. The last piece, “Brief Whistling” is just that, something straight out of a Morricone Western, Cinecittà suddenly rolling over the graves of unnamed soldiers.

Fans of lowkey drone and the cinematic side of ambient work should find plenty to scratch that itch. Others interested in the otherworldly beauty of the ondes Martenot should probably tune in too.

items._cn_summary: Accident Fantôme是由两组音乐人合作的长篇环境嗡鸣项目，在法国梅斯附近一座19世纪教堂内录制。专辑以管风琴为核心，辅以吉他、竖琴及早期电子乐器奥恩弦（ondes Martenot）——后者曾被梅西安、布莱兹等法国作曲家青睐。音乐呈现典型的drone-ambient美学：单一和弦持续震动，回响充斥空旷的教堂空间，嗡鸣质感厚实绵长。作品带有浓郁的暗氛围色彩，录制地点临近一战前线，地理与历史语境为声响增添了沉重感。乐评指出其声音氛围虽引人入胜但略显熟悉，末曲借鉴莫里康内西部片风格，形成跨类型参照。整体而言，这是融合当代古典、实验电子与暗氛围的跨界之作，适合偏好深层声响探索的听众。

items.body: Born in science-fiction novels and developed in philosophy and theoretical physics departments, the " Bootstrap Paradox " is a thought experiment about time travel. It's most easily explained in Back To The Future . Marty McFly, having travelled back in time from 1985 to 1955, finds himself shredding on electric guitar onstage at a school dance, a few months before anyone has ever heard of rock music. Offstage, a man yells into a phone: "Chuck! It's your cousin, Marvin Berry! You know that new sound you're lookin' for? Well, listen to this!" Chuck Berry, of course, is the Missouri singer and guitar player widely credited with inventing rock & roll. So, to summarise. In this alternative history, Chuck Berry hears rock & roll from a kid who heard about it from him . The core idea is this: were time travel possible, it would generate loop-points in time, scrambling the relationship between the past and the future. It's a deeply Spekki Webu move to choose this as an album title. The Dutch DJ and producer, who once described his music as "an intergalactic language that connects people and energies together," has always woven some element of sci-fi mysticism into his music. He's not alone. This is a time-honoured tradition we can trace from Sun Ra to the Electrifying Mojo to Underground Resistance and beyond. In fact, the first track here even shares a title with a Drexciya classic, "Wave Jumper." That said, these retro vibes do not extend to the music itself. Webu's own "Wave Jumper" is a strikingly modern and original piece of music that you can just barely call techno. With a yo-yo-ing, halftime beat at something closer to gabber tempo, and a general aura that's more skate video than warehouse rave. The rest of the album is equally adventurous, and it very much feels like club music's farther vanguard. Less than half the music on Bootstrap Paradox has the kind of galloping 4/4 chug you expect to hear in a nightclub (and to be fair, one of them clocks in at a soaring 153 BPM, beyond the reach of a turntable pitch shifter from most techno records). The rest floats on artfully off-kilter grooves that unfold like origami. Classic genre tropes are thin on the ground. Even the drums are abstract, with none of the sonic links to the physical realm that exist in most club music (no rim shots, no hi-hats, no snares, etc.). The sound design, meanwhile, summons a place both radically futuristic and deeply surreal, a cyberpunk vista through which strange bodies hover, at once abstract and weirdly physical, as if shaped from matter at some confusing middle point between solid, liquid and gas. Radical and mind-bendingly out-there, if not quite avant-garde, Bootstrap Paradox skips any pretense of being arty or experimental in favour of a vibe much closer to the heart of rave culture: trippy, alien and just plain fuckin' badass. In its most conventional moments, Bootstrap Paradox serves up dreamily transportive techno mantras. It's an effect best embodied by "Floating In Acheron," a nine-minute tribal tear-out named after one of the five rivers of the Underworld in Greek mythology. "Moments," the mellowest track here, has the dark soul of illbient artists like DJ Spooky, burying its outline of a beat deep in its ambient murk. The best bits come when we wade further out in the nether-regions, the in-between spaces of rhythm and tempo that few artists explore and that Spekki Webu knows so well. "Axis Point" is an elegantly off-kilter, slow-mo stepper whose groove takes two bars to fully unfold. The album reaches its climax on the final track, "Goodbye Universe," a broken-beat-ish thing that sounds in places like it was played live, off the grid—namely the backwards drum fills that slip just far enough out of time to be both jarring and funky. While the Hague artist might be a lifelong raver, Spekki Webu is still a relatively new artist: he only started DJing in the 2010s and releasing music in the last few years. That might be surprising if you know his records or his DJ sets, both of which have the technique and daring style of a seasoned pro. His music has come thick and fast since his first EP in 2023, and Neural Network , his first album, came out last May. That he's back barely a year later with an even stronger record shows the extraordinary depth of talent at play. On Bootstrap Paradox we hear an artist operating on his own weird frequency, vaulting to the farthest limits of techno and finding incredible things there.
items._cn_summary: Spekki Webu 是一位荷兰电子音乐制作人，《Bootstrap Paradox》以时间旅行悖论为概念框架，呈现出一张极具实验性的电子专辑。音乐风格虽被归入广义上的电子/techno，但实际更接近IDM与实验电子的交汇地带：节拍不拘一格，时而以gabber速度弹跳，时而以半拍律动漂浮；鼓组高度抽象化，剔除了常规军鼓与hi-hat等俱乐部标志元素。整体声音设计充满赛博朋克式的未来感与超现实氛围，介于Drexciya的太空感与滑板影像美学之间。专辑在保持俱乐部音乐核心律动感的同时，大幅拓展了声响的实验边界，展现出鲜明的个人辨识度与概念深度。

items._cn_summary: 这张原声带来自丹佛四人组Blood Incantation，是一部关于该乐队的电影配乐作品。乐评将其音乐定位在死亡金属与氛围音乐、模拟合成器、前卫摇滚及宇宙摇滚（Kosmische）的交汇处，特别提及了对Popul Vuh和Tangerine Dream等氛围与实验音乐前辈的深厚继承。2024年专辑《Absolute Elsewhere》以融合宣泄式死亡金属与出人意料的氛围段落、复杂前卫乐段而著称，被评为近十年来重型音乐领域最奇特且最具原创性的作品之一。这张原声带延续了这一跨界实验路线，将对外部与内心空间的探索编织进配乐框架，在极端金属骨架上嫁接了合成器氛围、宇宙摇滚质感与严肃的世界观构建。

items.body: Is it possible to protect a family member from the horrors of war? This question was posed in the film “Life Is Beautiful,” which inspired Ukrainian artist Halyna Andrusenko to create her own works of art, which in turn inspired the documentary by Joel Espi and the score by Daniela Mars, and whose title is shared by the opening track. Since the early days of the invasion, Ukrainians have been wrapping monuments and statues in cloth and reinforcing them with sandbags to protect them from fire and bombs. In her art, Andrusenko does the same with her family (allowing them to breathe of course) and draws sketches of them: a brand of performance art translated to physical form. Through flute and wordless voice, Mars conveys feelings of love and protection, with a melancholy undercurrent that highlights the fragility of human life. “Life Is Beautiful” is short yet sweet, a choral preface to the overture. Mars’ multitracked voice becomes that of a church choir, blurring the lines between baptism and requiem. Threaded into the following piece, the voice becomes the accompaniment for an array of flutes, operating as an additional instrument. Even without seeing the film, one can imagine the tenderness shown by Andrusenko as she wraps her family fold by fold, and the mixed feelings as she ties the cloth in string. “Colours of the Bending River” operates in the lower register, a cluster of dark thoughts. “Dana Nobis Pacem” (“Give Us Peace”) cements the spiritual connection. Part of the Latin Mass, the phrase also appears in works by Beethoven and Vaughn Williams. This prayer leads to the first of three versions of “Halyna’s Theme,” which is also the first of two contrabass pieces that represent the album’s emotional center. The contrabass take on “Dark Sky Lullaby” conjures images of its title; in Ukraine, these skies are as often caused by war as by weather. “In the Sky” is the score’s most abstract piece, a shimmer of dismay including a disturbing rustle at 00:50. Light and dark continue to battle, Mars’ voice a perennial reminder of hope. The later tracks grow more intimate with the sound of breath. “Halyna’s Theme (by the water)” offers early confidence, communicated by multiple flutes, before one steps to the fore, is heard and is then joined again, a parable of community. “Dark Sky” is balanced by “Silent Light,” the title a sideways allusion to “Silent Night.” We don’t know how the film ends, because we don’t know how or if the invasion ends. We do know that the war will leave a residue of sorrow. Mars conveys this beautifully in “The Wind Breathes,” leaving us with the bittersweet feeling of a mother who does what she can, knowing that it can never be enough. (Richard Allen) If you are in Kyiv, be sure to check out the exhibition, which just opened at the Dymchuk Gallery run by Max aka Trinidad Shevron!
items._cn_summary: Daniela Mars为乌克兰艺术家Halyna Andrusenko的纪录片创作配乐，主题围绕战时用布料包裹家人这一行为艺术展开。音乐以长笛、无词人声与低音提琴为核心，多轨人声模拟合唱团声效，营造出从洗礼到安魂的仪式氛围。专辑融合当代古典、氛围音乐与东欧文化语境，引入拉丁弥撒片段（Da Nobis Pacem），在战争阴影下探讨保护、脆弱与希望的命题。低音提琴演绎的主题曲与暗黑天空摇篮曲构成情感重心，抽象声响与呼吸质感贯穿全作。整体定位介于当代古典配乐与实验氛围音乐之间，具有鲜明的乌克兰战争文化视角和独特的概念框架。

items.body: Meanwhile, Artaud Seth and Ashley Dayour have been active as Near Earth Orbit (N.E.O.) for more than ten years and have built up an impressive discography. With this latest work, they once again delve into dystopian themes that, unfortunately, seem to be drawing ever closer to reality. This time, the focus lies on controlled chaos, manipulation, and rebellion within an authoritarian world order, inspiring the duo to craft nine compelling tracks. Musically, the band remains faithful to its distinct and idiosyncratic style: dark and often obscure, with guitars and electronics perfectly balanced and reinforcing one another with remarkable intensity. All of this is crowned by a charismatic voice that is impossible to ignore. N.E.O. does not necessarily impose a message upon the listener, yet a powerful sense of urgency and energy radiates throughout both the music and the vocals. The result is an overwhelming experience in which Industrial influences and epic arrangements guide us into a seemingly endless universe of terror. Several tracks also incorporate subtle EBM elements, particularly within the bass lines, further enhancing the aggressive and unsettling atmosphere. At times, this evolves into a truly Cinematic experience, though the band consistently maintains a perfect equilibrium between all these influences. As far as I am concerned, this stands among the band’s strongest and most polished albums to date: a complete concept work, accompanied once again by strikingly dark and artistic artwork. (Rating:8). Listen to “The Purge”: https://nearearthorbit.bandcamp.com/track/the-purge
items._cn_summary: Near Earth Orbit（Artaud Seth与Ashley Dayour的长期合作项目）发表的概念专辑，以反乌托邦为核心主题，描绘极权秩序下的操控与反抗。音乐风格横跨暗潮、工业与EBM三大领域，电吉他与电子合成器构成均衡的音色骨架，低音线条中融入了EBM的节奏特征，整体呈现出黑暗、压抑且具有史诗感的氛围。编曲展现出一定的电影化叙事倾向，元素层次丰富但保持内部平衡。专辑由德国独立厂牌Solar Lodge发行，乐评来源Side-Line为暗潮/工业领域具有公信力的专业媒体，对该作品给予8/10的高度评价，认定其为乐队迄今最成熟完整的概念作品之一。

items._cn_summary: Maryam Saleh 是埃及另类音乐场景中的重要人物，这张暌违八年的专辑《Syrr》由世界音乐权威杂志 Songlines 推介。来自中东地区的另类音乐人本身就是稀缺资源，其作品通常将阿拉伯传统音乐元素与另类、实验乃至前卫的手法相融合，跨越地域与流派的边界。埃及另类音乐场景历来注重诗歌性与政治性的表达，常在传统阿拉伯旋律结构中注入摇滚、电子或自由即兴的色彩。然而，提供的乐评内容仅为开篇片段，信息极为有限，无法深入评估该专辑具体的编曲手法、声音设计及创新程度。仅凭已知信息可判断其在世界音乐与实验音乐的交叉地带具有较高探索价值，但完整的艺术定位与独特性仍需更详尽的评论来佐证。

items._cn_summary: Tuuletar是一支来自芬兰的四重奏组合，以'人声民谣嘻哈'自居。专辑《Maammo》延续了他们将芬兰-乌戈尔语系传统和声与人声打击（beatboxing）相融合的路线，辅以俏皮的人声处理技巧。这种将北欧少数民族音乐根源与节奏性人声技巧结合的手法，在世界音乐范畴中具有较高的辨识度与实验性。芬兰属于非主流音乐地区，其乌戈尔语系传统本身具有独特的文化视角，人声作为唯一乐器的方式也体现了跨领域融合的思路。不过原文内容极为简短，无法深入了解专辑具体的编曲细节、制作水准及艺术深度，信息量不足以做出更全面的判断。

items.body: Vida, the third release by Dani Jané (Spanish guitar, loops, synthesizer, composition), is a lyrical, rhythmically driven title that combines elements of flamenco, Catalan folk, classical music, jazz, and Catalan and U.S. poetry. A graduate of the Conservatori Superior de Música del Liceu (Barcelona), Jané pursued further study (classical, flamenco, jazz, tango) elsewhere in Spain, and in Germany, France, Italy, and India. Among others, Jané has worked with the flamenco fusion ensemble Tío Montero, flautist Neus Plana Turu, and singers Manuel Araya, Marta Casals, Rusó Sala, and Giulietta Vidal. Marcel Torres (second guitar, effects), Pablo Giménez (transverse flute or side-blown flute, Andean panpipe, percussion), and percussionist Pulmon Beatbox accompany Jané on Vida. Backing the core quartet are flamenco singer Pere Martínez, bassist Tomàs Pujol, and drummer-percussionist Martí Hosta. While studying in Berlín, Jané composed "Preludi" and "El vol de la Vida," conceived as a classical suite of two movements; about four minutes in, the latter concludes with Martínez's keening bulerías, with passages from Walt Whitman's Song of Myself (sung in Spanish-language translation). "Clara" sets up a subtle interplay between Jané's guitar and Gimenez on flute, over a subdued but insistent bass and percussion foundation. Jané's grandfather Miquel Castanys wrote the lyrics to "Les penes de l'amor" (the pain of love) in 1938, adapted to a rumba Jané composed during his Berlin sojourn, in tribute to a forebearer Jané knows only through family stories, photos, and his grandfather's verses. "Lau" presents another guitar-flute encounter accented by understated effects and percussion. Jané composed the instrumental "Milonga C.F. 2.0" with reference to his parents' home, C.F., i.e., Can Finestres, in the province of Girona, where he spent his early years and first studied with a local guitarist. "Lydda," a tanguillos by Barcelona's Toti Soler (whom Jané cites as a major influence), wraps the album, wherein guitar and flute trade licks accented with Carnatic-like vocal percussion. Vida gives voice to a new generation of conservatory trained Catalan artists for whom flamenco is but one among myriad influences.
items._cn_summary: 西班牙吉他手Dani Jané的第三张专辑《Vida》融合了佛朗明哥、加泰罗尼亚民谣、古典音乐、爵士及世界音乐元素，呈现出多元文化交汇的个人美学。Jané拥有巴塞罗那里赛奥高等音乐学院的科班背景，并在西班牙、德国、法国、意大利及印度深造，作品中可见印度卡纳提克式人声打击乐的痕迹。专辑以吉他loop与合成器为媒介，串联诗歌文本（惠特曼及家族旧作）与多种节奏形态——包括布里亚斯、伦巴、米隆加与探戈。Marcel Torres、Pablo Giménez等乐手参与的编制丰富了器乐层次与即兴空间。整体定位介于当代作曲与世界融合之间，代表了新一代加泰罗尼亚音乐人对传统的重新诠释。

items.body: Loss galvanizes, loss focuses, and musical artists turn loss into shared reflections. Emi Makabe has focused the passing of her father into a generous meditation on resilience and legacy with her second recording on Sunnyside Records, Echo. The title reminds us of the connections between generations. Here are ten musical memories that span time and culture, blending a modern jazz sensibility with a traditional Japanese soul. Born in Japan, where she studied Japanese traditional music, Emi Makabe moved to New York in 2008. She is an educator and contributor to the jazz scene, composing and performing her own music. Her previous recordings, an EP on the Japanese Jazz label D-Musica Out of Time (2016) and Anniversary (2020), laid the foundation of her sound: soaring, sweet singing in Japanese, English and wordless vocalizing, accompanied by her flute and shamisen on top of jazz-inspired piano, drums, and double bass. Using these materials, Makabe celebrates the legacy of her father, supported by Thomas Morgan (double bass, backing vocals) and Vitor Gonçalves (piano, accordion, Wurlitzer electric piano), both of whom return from her previous records, as well as Kenny Wollesen (drums, percussion, vibraphone, electronics). Also appearing as guests are Meshell Ndegeocello (spoken word), Jason Moran (piano), and Bill Frisell (acoustic guitar) on the opening track. Opening with Frisell's acoustic guitar and confidently sentimental, "Birthday Song" comes to grips with loss, featuring a touching spoken meditation and a haunting Frisell solo. It ends with the hope, "I wanna remember the warmth of being in your arms." The record closes with "Overture," anchored by Gonçalves' dripping Wurlitzer supporting Makabe's Japanese exhortation, "Let's talk again, countless times/Let's talk, if we meet again." Besides the refreshingly unselfconscious sentimentality, Makabe strides confidently between the traditional Japanese melodies, instruments, and the language of her upbringing in her father's world and the contemporary jazz of New York clubs. "Snow" begins with Makabe's shamisen playing a pentatonic tune, while "Text" swings in a fast bebop, with Makabe's flute and harmonized Japanese scat singing. "Morisan" hurries between worlds led by bouncy accordion, rolling jazz traps, and a stylish piano solo by Jason Moran. Moran also shares production credits with Thomas Morgan and Makabe herself. Utterly unique in approach, and equipped with a lovely vocal instrument, and with a skilled and single-minded ensemble, Emi Makabe has created a passionate, introspective, and honest fusion of tradition and modernity to celebrate the passing of the generations.
items._cn_summary: Emi Makabe的第二张专辑《Echo》由独立厂牌Sunnyside Records发行，以父亲离世为创作主题，融合日本传统音乐与现代爵士。Makabe使用日语演唱、三味线与长笛等传统乐器，与爵士钢琴、低音提琴、鼓组及电钢琴合作，构建跨文化音乐对话。参与录制的乐手包括Thomas Morgan、Vitor Gonçalves、Kenny Wollesen、Jason Moran、Bill Frisell及Meshell Ndegeocello。作品横跨五声音阶民谣、bebop、抒情慢曲等多种形式，在传统日本旋律与纽约当代爵士语汇之间自由转换。整体呈现出东西方音乐传统的独特交融，以个人情感为纽带连接世代记忆，是一张兼具文化深度与爵士即兴精神的跨界作品。

items.body: Crete's Stelios Petrakis is at the peak of players of his island's best-known traditional instrument, the Cretan lyra, a small pear-shaped fiddle held vertically on the knee. Its three bowed strings are stopped by the fingernails of the non-bowing hand rather than being pressed to the fingerboard. Its sound hovers on the enticing edge between fundamental and harmonics. Petrakis is also a leading luthier, making the lyras and the other instruments he plays, including the traditional metal-strung lute laouto, and in conjunction with Ross Daly he's developed and plays a range of lyras with ringing sympathetic strings. True to its title, this an album of his lyra, and laouto, with a panoply of other traditional instruments played by musicians of equal stature to Petrakis, in music of rich lyricism, in melody and texture. "Astro Sti Gaza" ('Star in Gaza'), a wish for peace written by Petrakis with lyrics by his brother Yannis Petrakis, opens the album. At first a string drone, then Petrakis's laouto and lyra, Maëlle Duchemin's harp, Pavlos Spyropoulos's double bass, and the percussion of Iranian Bijan Chemirani, who plays frame and flask hand-drums on most tracks. The dark, sinuous instrumental line is tracked by the husky vocal of Giorgis Xylouris, who sings on three tracks, the other six being instrumental. "Nathenas," a traditional Cretan song in asymmetric rhythms, has a powerful ensemble of lyra, laouto, frame-drum, stick-hit davul, topped out by Breton Sylvain Barou's reeds and Armenian shvi whistle. "Anglianico," a stately melody composed by Petrakis, has the tremolo mandolins of Valencian musician Efrén López and Michalis Kontaxakis in an elegant almost orchestral sound with lyra, guitars (Antonis Voumvoulakis and Samuel Mele), Spyropoulos's double bass, and the accordion of Mattia Marco Gregoriadis on whose improvisation the tarantella-like "Pukanè" is based. Chemirani is particularly featured on his composition "Panj Pol," a short finger-rippling, slapping solo on zarb flask-drum whose rhythm is the foundation for the song that it breaks into, "Agrilos," by Petrakis with lyrics by brother Yannis celebrating the wine-producing district of Crete where they grew up. It develops into a big sound of massed instruments, with a break on frame-drum and Sakir Oran Uygan's big double-headed davul drum before a surge of squealing tulum bagpipe and other wind instruments from Barou. "Evlerin Önü Mersin," a traditional tune from Asia Minor, has a march-like feel, beginning with keening lyra over a slow, inexorable drum pulse, building to soaring epic as more instruments join, peaking with Barou's zurnas. "Muixeranga," again with a steady, imposing pulse, is an anthemic tune played in Valencia during the Muixeranga, the traditional building of excitingly high pyramidal human towers in which the big and strong form the bottom layers and the youngest and lightest clamber up to form the topmost. Petrakis intends the track as a message of support to Valencia following the climate-change-driven floods of 2024. Preluded and accompanied by ringing 3/4 time arpeggiating plucked strings and percussion, with the melody played on lyra, the source of "Nothing Else Matters," is unexpected: it's a beautiful version, evocative of memory and perhaps sadness, of a Metallica number.
items._cn_summary: 克里特岛里拉琴演奏家兼制琴师Stelios Petrakis的个人专辑，以希腊克里特传统音乐为核心，汇聚了来自布列塔尼、亚美尼亚、伊朗、瓦伦西亚、意大利及土耳其等多国音乐人参与。专辑以克里特里拉琴与laouto琉特为主线，搭配zurnas管乐器、zarb手鼓、davul双面鼓、shvi哨笛及手风琴等丰富传统乐器，形成跨地域的世界音乐融合。曲目涵盖原创与改编的传统曲调，旋律性强，注重各文化声部间的对话。Petrakis与Ross Daly合作开发带共鸣弦的里拉琴，体现了乐器创新。整体定位为传统根基扎实、跨文化协作丰富的世界音乐作品，在传统性与多元融合之间取得平衡，但实验性与前卫色彩相对有限。

items.body: I want to personally direct you to a remarkable piece of music titled "Two Views of a Prayer," composed and written by David Dzubinski as part of the Prism Quartet's new series of collaborations called Unlocking Your Inner Composer. If you have listened to my radio programs, you are probably familiar with the quartet's ground-breaking, genre-blurring music. If not, there's no better introduction than this. Performed in November of 2025 at the Free Library of Philadelphia, they invited vocalist Ursula Rucker, percussionist Tyshawn Sorey, and violinist Carlos Santiago to collaborate on the arrangement and performance of Dzubinski's composition. It travels from raw to lyrical and back in the course of just under 4 minutes, with both finesse and energy. - Cliff Furnald, editor Find Prism Quartet online. items._cn_summary: 这是由Prism Quartet（萨克斯四重奏）联合打击乐家Tyshawn Sorey、口语诗人Ursula Rucker及小提琴家Carlos Santiago合作演出的当代新作品《Two Views of a Prayer》，由David Dzubinski作曲。作品以不到四分钟的篇幅，在粗粝即兴与抒情段落之间快速切换，融合了室内乐编制、实验打击乐与口语/吟唱元素，体现出强烈的跨界意识。Prism Quartet一向以打破流派边界著称，Sorey更是当代实验音乐领域的重要人物，二者合作使该作品在学院派新音乐与自由即兴之间找到了交叉点。RootsWorld作为以世界音乐和实验音乐为导向的独立平台推荐此作。整体属于短小精炼的跨流派实验作品，融合度高但内容信息有限，缺乏对作品技法与结构的深入分析。

items.body: After nine previous albums and a 25-year career at the forefront of world music, Lucas Santtana is fluent in the many genres of Brazilian music. His new project, Brasiliano, is a musical exploration of the languages of Brazil. With songs sung in Portuguese, French, English, Spanish, Occitan, Cape Verde Creole, and Tupy-Guarani, a Brazilian native language, Santtana has assembled guest lyricists and vocalists representing a range of musical and linguistic influences. The result is a warm and compelling musical treatise on the diverse cultural history of Brazil, expressed through the Brazilian variant of Portuguese, best described as Brasiliano. Returning to his roots, the opening cut and lead single "A história de nossa língua" features Gilberto Gil, a national treasure with whom Santtana worked early in his career. As the liner notes explain, Brasiliano, the language, is depicted in the song as a feminine character meeting other people (languages) on her travels, tracing the history of the language as an offshoot of Latin, including "Occitan, Celtic, Galician, Portuguese, Mozarabic, and others. The chorus features Indigenous words that are part of everyday Brazilian culture: Itapuã, Ipanema, Maracanã, Capoeira, etc." This song acts as a sort of abstract for the dissertation to follow. Santtana and Gil call and respond over what has become the composer's trademark mixture of detailed, layered, human-played instruments, including on this track violins and violas, piano, guitars, mellotron, and synths. Throughout the record, Santtana creates an inviting effect with a contemporary gloss, combined with the warm resonance of wood, drum skins, wire strings, sticks, bows, and voices. The album features a range of styles, from the lively party track "Ver meu povo se abraçar" to the convincing reggae of the second single, "Que seja um reggae". With sophisticated songcraft and inspired arrangements, the songs remain inviting and accessible.

items._cn_summary: 这张巴西音乐人Lucas Santtana的专辑以'巴西的语言'为主题，通过葡萄牙语、法语、英语、西班牙语、奥克语、佛得角克里奥尔语及图皮-瓜拉尼语等七种语言的歌曲，呈现巴西多元文化的历史脉络。专辑邀请Gilberto Gil等客座音乐人参与，融合小提琴、中提琴、钢琴、吉他、键盘琴及合成器等多种乐器，在传统手作质感与现代制作光泽之间取得平衡。风格涵盖欢快的派对曲风、雷鬼节拍及文化叙事歌曲，以精致编排和可听性为特点，属于有学术深度的世界融合音乐。

items.body: The newly released album from Malian musicians Neba Solo and Benego Diakité is the outcome of a project which began in 2013 when Solo and Diakité, playing balafon and n'goni respectively, were recorded by Bamako producer Ousmane Haïdara. He played the result to another record producer, Nick Gold, who was completely taken by what he heard and together they decided to work on the recording to produce a finished album, also enlisting English musician Sonny Johns to help with the production. Gold had previously brought together Ali Farka Touré and Toumani Diabaté to record what was to become the very successful album In the Heart of the Moon and this was a similar story, Solo and Diakité also being established Malian musicians coming from different musical backgrounds. Indeed, the balafon and n'goni, though both widely associated with Malian music, are seldom played together. A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking, released as a double CD, is very much an album of two halves. The recordings made in 2013 of the two musicians playing together were transformed over time into ensemble arrangements with the addition of other musicians playing strings, mellotron, guitar and percussion, plus overdubbed vocals from Solo and three female singers. These reworked tracks make up the first half of the album. The opening track, "Djinê Mogo Tiki" begins with a capella backing vocals before Diakité introduces a repeated riff on the n'goni over which Solo improvises on the balafon while also taking the lead vocal, a pattern which forms the basis of all the tracks, with the augmented instrumentation creating further layers of interest. "Djinê Mogo Tiki" is one of two tracks to have strings added and these sit well, used sparingly to provide short rhythmic motifs, thankfully belying any fears that might be raised by mention of a string arrangement. The reinvention of these pieces, clearly done with the co-operation of both Solo and Diakité, may be radical but it has nevertheless been carried out with consideration and musical sensibility. "Yeredon Bali" begins with a few phrases from Solo's balafon, to be joined by Diakité's n'goni, some light percussion and hand claps and then more of the female backing vocals, supporting Solo's vocal in the call and response style characteristic of so much Mande music. In this case the vocal content is the only significant addition to the original duo recording, but significant it is because, in the nature of things, once a vocal line is added that becomes the main focus of attention. What makes the format of this album particularly intriguing is that the final six tracks give us the opportunity of hearing the original, unadorned versions of most of the arranged tracks as first recorded by Neba Solo and Benego Diakité. They are referred to as the "Garden Demos" since they were recorded in a Bamako garden under a mango tree. Without the added vocals the focus shifts to the interplay between the two musicians, and the meaning of the music changes. "Djine Mogo Tiki (Garden Demo excerpt) For example, we are offered two versions of "Djinê Mogo Tiki," first appearing as the album's opening track in its arranged version, then later in the original duo take. Perhaps this has been done to show two sides of the same story, with an awareness too of differences in what audiences are looking for. The arranged tracks, with their instrumental variety and vocal additions, certainly work well and might help give the music wider appeal. But if you are someone who is captivated by listening to fine players engaged in a musical conversation, eavesdropping on the almost telepathic interaction taking place as the two musicians explore the common ground between them, then it's really already there in the earlier Garden Demos, the final six tracks of A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由马里音乐家Neba Solo（巴拉风琴）与Benego Diakité（恩戈尼）合作，由曾促成Ali Farka Touré与Toumani Diabaté合作的制作人Nick Gold操刀完成。专辑以双CD形式发行，前半部分为2013年原始录音经重新编配的合奏版本，加入弦乐、mellotron、吉他、打击乐与多声部人声层次；后半部分为"花园录音"原始二重奏版本，呈现曼丁哥音乐典型的即兴对话结构。两种版本构成有趣的对照：前者展示了传统乐器在当代制作框架中的拓展，后者让听者聚焦于两位演奏家纯粹的交织与呼应。巴拉风琴与恩戈尼的罕见组合，以及对原始素材审慎而克制的再造手法，使专辑在世界音乐范畴中呈现出独到的艺术构思与文化底蕴。

items.body: Tariq Goddard dodges the punches and negotiates with arthritis in order to bear witness to one for the ages I remember the shock at discovering that Marlene Dietrich was still alive in 1992. She lived long enough to have raised a glass with Brecht and listened to all but one of Kraftwerk’s albums; and if she hadn't been careful, ample time to take in Klaus Kinski and The Scorpions as well. Perhaps sensing that contemporaneity would eventually kill her, Dietrich wisely locked the door and refused to read the papers, an option that does not exist for innovators whose enduring relevance requires meeting their public. I feel something of the same era-straddling incongruity watching Kraftwerk play live in 2026 in Bournemouth,... The post Europe Eternal: Kraftwerk in Bournemouth appeared first on The Quietus.
items._cn_summary: Kraftwerk 是电子音乐的先驱与标志性乐队，其声响融合了合成器序列、节拍编程与极简主义美学，横跨 electro、techno、ambient 等多个电子分支，对 IDM 与实验电子产生了深远影响。本文为 Kraftwerk 2026 年在英国伯恩茅斯演出现场的乐评，发表于独立音乐媒体 The Quietus。作者以独特的文化视角切入，将 Kraftwerk 置于跨时代艺术家的语境中，与玛琳·黛德丽等历史人物并置，探讨经典艺术家在新时代现场演出中的延续性与不适感。文章文风文学性强，但正文信息量有限，对音乐本身的音色设计、曲目编排、舞台呈现等具体细节涉及较少，更侧重于文化评论与个人感受。整体而言属于电子音乐领域中对传奇艺术家的现场回顾，与实验/电子音乐偏好有一定契合度。

items._cn_summary: Purgate是加拿大裔法国音乐人Frédéric Arbour的个人实验电子/暗环境项目，作品《Leavings》由其主理的厂牌Aesthetical以CD与数字形式发行。Aesthetical专注于实验电子领域，Arbour同时也是知名暗潮/暗环境厂牌Cyclic Law及Cavsas的创始人，并以Stärker、Visions等多个别名进行创作，在地下实验音乐圈资历深厚。《Leavings》属于暗潮与实验电子交叉范畴的独奏作品，与暗环境、氛围音乐及工业电子等审美取向高度相关。然而原文为新闻简讯性质，内容在介绍厂牌背景后即被截断，缺少对作品音色、结构、创作意图及具体听感层面的实际评述，信息量不足以构成完整乐评。整体来看，该项目在风格定位上与暗潮/实验电子听众的偏好契合，但因内容深度不足，仅能作为发行资讯参考。

items.album: David A. Jaycock :: Children of the Cold War [Phase 7] (Subexotic)
items.excerpt: This is not merely an album about pessimism, collapse, paranoia, or sepia memories. It is an expertly crafted and beautifully sustained paean to the enduring presence of the motion of Goodness—often obscured, often wounded, not-for-profit, but somehow still capable of outliving every system designed to extinguish it. A balm for balmy days and long dark nights of the soul. The suggestion that love remains the brightest survivor Children of The Cold War: Phase 7 by david a jaycock   Reflectin
items.body: This is not merely an album about pessimism, collapse, paranoia, or sepia memories. It is an expertly crafted and beautifully sustained paean to the enduring presence of the motion of Goodness—often obscured, often wounded, not-for-profit, but somehow still capable of outliving every system designed to extinguish it. A balm for balmy days and long dark nights of the soul. The suggestion that love remains the brightest survivor Children of The Cold War: Phase 7 by david a jaycock   Reflecting a conceptual framework deeply familiar to me as a generational conceit—Cold War nihilism and the erstwhile apocalyptic triptych—David A. Jaycock channels Children of the Cold War [Phase 7] with remarkable emotional precision, beautifully building on his frankly magnificent, intelligent discography thus far. The spectral ache of “Raymond Briggs’ When the Wind Blows” lingers throughout this musical equivalent: a work that captures both the naïveté and fragile beauty of the human waltz when refracted through that same recurring self-sabotaging hubris—the assumption that humanity alone are the rightful architects of profit alone, war, where we are seen functioning primarily as an economy disguised as an ideology of safety or rescue. As a result, a soulful, melancholic humility is woven throughout the album’s musical palette. There is sadness here. There is a deeper knowing that belies the intent. Jaycock understands, through lived experience, the emotional residue left behind by generations raised beneath the abstract possibility of absolute annihilation. The album is a reflection of that. Sonically, the tracks evoke those same BBC Sound Effects themes and atmospheres: enormous synthesis, tender tonality, vast reverbs, and big drums carry a cinematic weight without ever surrendering their innate intimate fragility. Melodies tenderly strum, and arpeggiations roll and coil gently; tempos remain calm, measured, almost comforting—and that restraint ultimately strengthens the conceptual brilliance of the work. It is an exceptionally well-executed, collated duality of paradox: human advancement through its own experience in real time. Tracks such as the beatific opener “Circling the Church,” or track three’s synth-pop-inflected “Butterflies Disco,” recall the emotional architecture of early DinDisc-era OMD before the hairstyles, presets, and pop polish calcified the aesthetic. There is an overt sincerity in the open-hearted circuitry. There is vulnerability inside the man-machine. For me, the standout on my second listen is “Secret Bunkers Under Civic Centres,” where colossal synth textures form a glowing, miasmic wall of oranges and yellows, through which warm winds carry a delicious rolling synth figure bearing faint flute-like traces of BoC-style pastoral dislocation. But that possibly inhibitory simile is merely a reflection of a similar DNA through the cultural mores and timeframe of history itself—a generational propensity lost elsewhere. Echoes of an imagined dystopia that never truly disappeared :: The warmth of the album becomes iridescent and undeniable, neatly juxtaposing echoes of an imagined dystopia that never truly disappeared—and has now resurfaced in its attempts to profit from newer forms, as the money machine liquefies into the empty form it has always been: a resource for life more than the very reason to live it. I remember the inherited threat of doom. I remember the awareness of the capitalist machinery beneath it all—the arms trade swelling quietly beneath public language and political theatre. Yet despite the ever-present duality of darkness and light, fear and tenderness, Children of the Cold War is an example that ultimately arrives at something profoundly giving that cannot be bought, and is more human: the suggestion that love remains the brightest survivor. And wins. And in that sense, this is not merely an album about pessimism, collapse, paranoia, or sepia memories. It is an expertly crafted and beautifully sustained paean to the enduring presence of the motion of Goodness—often obscured, often wounded, not-for-profit, but somehow still capable of outliving every system designed to extinguish it. A balm for balmy days and long dark nights of the soul. Children of the Cold War [Phase 7] is available on Subexotic. [Bandcamp] Children of The Cold War: Phase 7 by david a jaycock

items.album: Shimmering in the Dark: How Duo Solipse Reimagines the Night Through Debussy’s Lens

items.body: Away from the grand orchestral stages and the heavy resonance of the piano, Elena Stojceska and Romain Petiot find a fragile, breathtakingly intimate nocturnal world in their new album, “Pour que la nuit…” Artist: Duo Solipse (Elena Stojceska: flute / Romain Petiot: guitar) Album: Pour que la nuit… Label: Solipse Records Release Date: June 5, 2026 Recorded at: Studio 150, Amsterdam (Sessions: April 2024) Sometimes, an album is not just a collection of recorded pieces, but the physical translation of a long, shared human journey. For Elena Stojceska and Romain Petiot—the minds and hands behind Duo Solipse—their latest release, Pour que la nuit…, is exactly that: the beautiful, hard-earned fruit of a deep companionship with the music of Claude Debussy, shaped over years, changing seasons, and different places. To build an entire album around Debussy using only a flute and a guitar feels beautifully audacious—mostly because Debussy never actually wrote a single note for this combination. Yet, listening to these tracks, recorded in the warm, quiet atmosphere of Amsterdam’s Studio 150, it feels like this music was always meant to live here, stripped of its traditional grandeur and laid bare. A Study in Black, White, and Iridescent Color The spark for this whole project was lit back in 2017, when a close friend of the duo, Vincent Airault, suggested a wild idea: arranging Prélude à l’après-midi d’un Faune for just flute and guitar. Elena and Romain admit they were skeptical at first. How do you translate a massive, glittering orchestral masterpiece into the quiet dialogue of two intimate acoustic instruments? They solved it by embracing the restriction. They turned the Prélude into a “black and white” study. By peeling away the heavy symphonic layers, they exposed a raw, fragile, and deeply human core. Curiously, they placed this track at the very end of the album, turning it into a circular ending—a sudden burst of daylight that casts a retrospective warmth over the entire night you just walked through. If the Prélude is about stripping away color, their rendition of the Six épigraphes antiques (arranged by Romain himself from the four-hand piano original) does the exact opposite. Here, the duo takes the stark “black and white” of the piano and transforms it into something iridescent and shimmering. The breathy warmth of the flute and the tactile pluck of the guitar strings create a dream-like landscape inspired by ancient myths and distant, idealized worlds, blurring the lines between what is real and what is imagined. From Modern Anxiety to Oceanic Peace The night, however, isn’t always peaceful, and the album doesn’t shy away from its darker, heavier corners. It opens with Edison Denisov’s Sonata, which feels like entering a restless, midnight cityscape. Through a dialogue filled with avant-garde sound effects and quarter-tones, the music mimics the subtle, unpredictable sounds of a nocturnal wildlife taking over the dark. Meanwhile, the guitar plods along imperturbably—a striking, almost ironic echo of our modern world, completely oblivious to the secret life that unfolds after hours. The perfect antidote to this tension comes through the music of Tōru Takemitsu, a composer who truly inherited Debussy’s spiritual obsession with nature. His piece Toward the Sea (originally commissioned by Greenpeace and performed here on the alto flute) is a gorgeous, immersive experience. Takemitsu weaves notes into what he called “the sea of tonality”. The music becomes fluid, wide, and spacious; the flute feels like a solitary wind blowing across dark, deep waters, carrying a cinematic weight that hits you straight in the chest. Intimate Solitudes In the middle of this journey, the duo steps back to give each other room for two haunting solo confessions. Romain takes on Manuel de Falla’s Homenaje, a piece written as a funeral tribute to Debussy. His guitar carries a heavy, austere Spanish grief that builds tension before melting into a distant musical quote. In response, Elena delivers Tomislav Zografski’s Invention “Syrinx”, a solo flute monologue that stands as a contemporary, lonely echo bouncing through the dark. The Verdict Pour que la nuit… is a profoundly honest album. It takes immense courage to take historical, academic classical masterpieces and play them with this level of vulnerability and space. Under the artistic direction of Daniel Rowland and captured beautifully by sound engineer Joeri Saal, the recording feels incredibly close—you can hear the wood, the breath, the fingers sliding on strings, and the quiet spaces in between. For the modern classical and ambient community, this is a record to be cherished. It’s a bridge between old-world impressionism and modern, cinematic sound design. Turn off the lights, close your eyes, and let this circular night wash over you. The post Shimmering in the Dark: How Duo Solipse Reimagines the Night Through Debussy’s Lens first appeared on Modern Classical Music.
items._cn_summary: Duo Solipse由长笛演奏家Elena Stojceska与吉他演奏家Romain Petiot组成，专辑《Pour que la nuit…》以德彪西作品的非常规改编为核心，辅以爱迪生·杰尼索夫的先锋奏鸣曲。长笛与吉他的组合是德彪西从未涉足的编制，二人将管弦乐织体剥离为两件原声乐器的私密对话，在单色冷峻与虹彩闪烁之间构建夜晚的声景。杰尼索夫奏鸣曲引入不安分的先锋音效与极端演奏技法，与德彪西的梦境化改编形成张力对比。专辑在阿姆斯特丹Studio 150录制，由二人自创的Solipse Records发行，是一张强调概念统一性与室内乐亲密感的小规模独立制作。整体定位介于当代古典与先锋跨界之间，对偏好实验声响与现代作曲的听众具有一定吸引力。

items.body: A war of words, They want you on their side, It’s all for power, To conquer and divide. Promises have a strange power: they ask us to believe in something that has not happened yet, turning a word given in the present into a bridge toward the future. At their best, they hold up friendships, love affairs, movements, contracts, countries, and songs — invisible, but load-bearing. But somewhere along the way, the promise became another tool of persuasion, polished into a slogan, stamped onto a product, fed through a corporate choir, and sold back to us under fluorescent light. Now promises arrive dressed in branding, panic, and performance, offered by people who profit when everyone else starts doubting the ground beneath their feet. The word remains, but the weight has changed: what once carried trust now often carries leverage. That crisis of faith runs through “World of Promises,” the new single from Scottish synthwave and synthpop artist Michael Oakley. The track appears on his new album Prologue, out now via NewRetroWave, and finds Oakley turning the bright machinery of retro-futurist pop toward something darker: a world of overstimulation, public fracture, and language drained of meaning. Musically, “World of Promises” moves with a sleek, late-night pressure: a seductive bass synth, compressed dance-floor stomp, warping metallic accents, cinematic pads, and Oakley’s silk-smooth vocal delivery cutting through the dry ice. The reference points are there — Depeche Mode, Pet Shop Boys, New Order, The Midnight, FM-84 — but Oakley pushes the track into a glossier, more high-stakes register, where synthpop romance meets corporate dread and the dance floor starts to look like a control room. Lyrically, “World of Promises” takes aim at false hope, weaponized messaging, corporate agendas, and the way public life turns people into factions. Oakley frames the song as a question of trust: “Do our words still mean a thing?” From there, the track spirals through cracked social bonds, power games, and the sense that every statement arrives with a hidden hand behind it. The song’s title becomes less a phrase of optimism than a warning label for an age built on empty guarantees. The video turns that idea into a neon-noir surveillance thriller. It opens inside a red-lit club world of dark glasses, glowing tubes, shadowed faces, and bodies caught in the blur of VHS damage. Oakley appears amid the party’s controlled chaos, while a red-haired woman in patterned sunglasses watches from above, then from a bank of monitors, studying security footage as if she were tracking a target through a private system of power. From there, the clip cuts between bound figures, gloved hands, a blindfolded man wrapped in rope, a silver briefcase, and a gun and martini left under club lights. The imagery plays like a retro cyber-crime caper spliced into a nightclub fever dream: CCTV grids, scan-mode graphics, coded data, red rooms, blue corridors, and sudden flashes of violence held back by the video’s stylized restraint. Captions break the tension with “WHOA. HEY!”, “THAT’S HER!”, and “STOP!!!” as the video’s mystery red-haired femme fatale, brandishing the silver briefcase, gives two men the slip—giving the clip the feel of the Tech Noir scene in The Terminator, The Starck Club scene in Robocop, or a late-night broadcast from a cult film aired on Nightflight. By the final stretch, the video widens into a chase for the woman with the case, moving through backstage rooms, club corridors, a logo wall, and a burst of falling papers. When her pursuer tries to vaporize her, the blast rebounds, turning the weapon back on him and leaving smoke curling around his boots as she slips outside to a waiting car. There, the case is opened for a man whose interest only deepens the mystery — a sly nod to the glowing, unknowable MacGuffin at the center of Quentin Tarantino’s Pulp Fiction. It is sleek, theatrical, and slightly absurd in the best way: part espionage fantasy, part nightclub power struggle, part commentary on who gets watched, who gives the orders, and who walks away with the prize. Watch the video for “World of Promises” below: Michael Oakley is a Scottish synthwave producer, songwriter, and musician whose work draws from synthpop, new wave, and widescreen 1980s studio craft. Born in Glasgow, Oakley moved to Los Angeles in 2016 before settling in Canada in 2018. A self-taught musician, he first broke through with the California EP in 2017, followed by his debut full-length, Introspect, in 2019 and Odyssey in 2021. Across his catalog, Oakley has become a key figure in the modern synthwave world, balancing polished pop songwriting with the romantic voltage of vintage machines. His work has appeared in gaming projects including Wave Break: High Tides and Retro Drive, and he has also designed sound packs and synth patches for producers working in the same retro-electronic orbit. With Prologue, Oakley returns after nearly five years with a sharper, bigger, and more politically charged sound. “Imagine what Depeche Mode’s Violator album would have sounded like if it was produced by Trevor Horn.” Says Oakley, “Or if Peter Hook stumbled into Haddaway’s recording sessions. That’s Prologue.” Michael Oakley’s new album Prologue is out now. Available in red and blue editions across multiple formats, including vinyl, cassette, CD, and MiniDisc. Order the album here. items.body: Oppenheimer MKII’s Oh! My Mind Is a Storm is paranoia rendered as pop machinery: compact, severe, oddly catchy, and built around the sense that the private mind has become a public emergency. The duo of Andy Oppenheimer, on lyrics and vocals, and Mahk Rumbae, on arrangements and production, work inside a strain of icy synth-pop that has always understood dread as a useful dance partner. Here, that dread is internalized, digitized, and sent back through the screen as a command. Mahk Rumbae’s production tightens around it with crunchy drums, rippling minimal synths, and ghostly pads that recall an eighties science-fiction serial caught between public-access television and a government transmission. Andy Oppenheimer’s soft-clipped delivery lands like a machine reciting beat poetry after reading too many classified reports. That sense of psychic pressure is the point. Oh! My Mind Is a Storm drives panic into club form, with Andy Oppenheimer declaring, ‘When I go dark, I’m into demon mode’. The line is funny, faintly ridiculous, and unnervingly current, catching the way contemporary anxiety often borrows the language of online performance. Demon mode becomes a state of overload, a persona, a coping mechanism, a threat. The accompanying video is deliberately austere: Andy Oppenheimer faces the camera, his head floating in greyscale, the image warped and reduced until he appears less like a performer than a transmission that has survived from some late-twentieth-century broadcast bunker. There is a touch of Max Headroom in the presentation, though drained of commercial smirk and turned into something more spectral: a pair of cathode-tube ghosts, bending time while barely moving at all. The minimalism suits the song. Nothing distracts from the faces, the voices, or the sense of a mind caught in feedback with itself. Watch below: The track also sharpens the broader concerns of Embrace The Dark, the long-awaited second album from Oppenheimer MKII, due June 30th via Wave Tension Records. Embrace The Dark does exactly as its title suggests: it welcomes dark, apocalyptic themes for our current turbulent times. In nine mind-blowing tracks, Mahk’s thunderous dance rhythms and addictive synth-pop melodies combine with Andy’s latest dystopian (and sometimes utopian) visions of our past, present and future. Andy Oppenheimer, formerly one-half of the cult 1980s synth-pop duo Oppenheimer Analysis, brings the clipped authority of the early minimal-synth era, while Mahk Rumbae, known for Codex Empire, Mitra Mitra, and Konstruktivists, gives the material a harder frame. Since their 2013 debut, The Presence of the Abnormal, Oppenheimer MKII have issued singles through Falco Invernale Records, Peripheral Minimal, and TONN Recordings. With “Oh! My Mind Is a Storm,” Oppenheimer MKII turns mental overload into a stark little broadcast from the edge of the future. Listen to Oh! My Mind Is a Storm below and order the album here. items.body: Back after a four-year absence, Dublin's Gilla Band have lost none of their bite, packing two songs into 'Giraffe': one noisy, dubbed-out slow burner and a grotty, dance-punk coda. items._cn_summary: Gilla Band是来自都柏林的四人乐队，时隔四年推出双曲作品《Giraffe》。音乐风格定位在后朋克与噪音摇滚的交汇处，融入dub回声质感与失真音效。A面为嘈杂、回响浓厚的慢速燃烧曲，B面则是粗粝的舞曲朋克收尾。乐队以主唱Dara Kiely的观察与困惑为核心文本，配合成员构建的倾斜节奏、失真层次与刺耳噪音声响。整体呈现出一定的实验倾向与噪音美学，但结构上仍属于摇滚框架内的拓展，未深入触及前卫电子、自由即兴或当代古典等领域。作为独立厂牌发行的作品，保留了地下音乐的反叛气质与粗砺质感。

items.body:
As the man at the controls at our label showcase at Public Records in 2024, our relationship working together had just started, and his new album ‘Immersion’ (released last month) was in mastering stages. After hearing his opening set, an isolatedmix was written in the stars. 

I technically heard Griff DJ at Brooklyn’s The Lot radio station just a few hours before our label showcase - sharing the booth with him as a temporary groupie while I plastered ASIP stickers all over the walls - and had been deep in his guest mixes prior to us even meeting in person. His journey as a DJ regularly takes him to festivals worldwide, and as part of his connection with Delayed , some intimate sets in the Pocono’s have come to fruition and are a worthy bookmark if you end up liking this one. 

As someone who can traverse a multitude of styles, from ambient and downtempo to deeper house and techno, Griff’s one of those artists that shows up in different ways - every time. Likely because, his music, and the stories around his reasons for his music, are often very personal. Whether it’s a concept, or a vibe, I get the feeling Griff is a master of sense and construct - a pretty special skill for an artist and DJ to have, where stories told come from the heart and have a pure reason. Not performance for performance sake, but a narrative traveling from the mind, told through a meticulous track selection. 

The concept was my attempt to portray various stages of consciousness throughout the morning, from dark into light / sleep to awake, as I get up & start the day & eventually get outside, into the woods for a morning - deep sleep into REM, vivid dreams, waking up from a dream & it's still dark outside but there's a faint glow of light, immersed in nature feeling the warmth of the sun in your face. It starts out cold, dark, alien, otherworldly then shifts towards something more mysterious & inviting but still a bit strange, then moves into warm & fuzzy. Analogous to frost on the ground slowly being melted, warmed & evaporated by the sun. - Aspetuck
